MARKET.head: Cruise lines become experiential sales channel for US wineries
MARKET.summ: From dedicated charters to custom bottlings, wineries are leveraging cruise partnerships to capture engaged audiences and drive long-term sales
takeaways: Cooper's Hawk Winery & Restaurant chartered Virgin Voyages' Valiant Lady for wine club members in 2024; the sold-out cruise led 30 percent of members to book a second sailing in February 2027.
Four Feathers Wine Services created a Columbia Valley sparkling wine for Holland America's fleet in 2024; it became the cruise line's most-served adult beverage across all ships.
Eleven Eleven Wines, a Napa boutique, hosted 60 guests on Scenic Eclipse II in the Mediterranean and achieved 33 percent conversion of non-members to wine club, plus two referrals.

MARKET.head: Vineyard operators idle acres to cut costs while awaiting market recovery
MARKET.summ: Rather than abandoning vineyards amidst declining demand, some grape growers are pressing pause with the hopes of resuming production in a few years
takeaways: A 2025 study of 19 northern Willamette Valley vineyards found idling reduced management costs by an average of 38 percent per acre, with some sites cutting costs in half.
Vineyard idling, a temporary halt to production lasting one to three years, preserves vines and capital rather than removal, allowing producers to survive current weak grape demand.
Viticulturists report idling requires careful maintenance including aggressive pruning, minimal irrigation, weed control, and selective fungicide spraying to revive vines when markets recover.

MARKET.head: Wildfires destroy 200 hectares in Sierra de Gredos wine region
MARKET.summ: The ethereal Garnachas of Sierra de Gredos have brought new recognition to this Spanish winemaking region, but after wildfires recently swept through the region, can the momentum continue?
takeaways: Between July 22 and 26, wildfires burned 77,000 hectares across Ávila and Madrid provinces, with approximately 200 hectares of vineyards in Cebreros DO damaged by fire or smoke, representing around 40 percent of registered vineyard area there.

Producers including Comando G's Daniel Landi and Juanan Martín of Rico Nuevo have drafted proposals to regional authorities requesting subsidies for forest clearance and firebreaks, along with support for vineyard planting and dry-stone wall restoration.

MARKET.head: Southern Glazer's pays $12.5M to settle DOJ bribery investigation
MARKET.summ: On Thursday, alcohol distributor Southern Glazer’s announced that it reached a resolution with the United States Department of Justice (DOJ) and the Alcohol and Tobacco Trade Bureau (TTB) in a longstanding investigation related to improper payments and bribery. In the deal, Southern agreed to pay $12.5 million.
takeaways: Southern Glazer's, the US alcohol distributor, reached a non-prosecution agreement with the DOJ and TTB on Thursday, resolving a bribery probe covering 2016-2024.
Former employees allegedly gave cash, gift cards, luxury goods, and trips to California retailers for better shelf placement; the company also issued false invoices to hide payments.
Southern Glazer's will pay $12.5 million and strengthen compliance controls over the next two years under the settlement terms.

MARKET.head: US tariff lift and India trade deal reshape Scotch whisky market in 2026
MARKET.summ: Is it possible that 2026 could eventually be looked back on as the make-or-break year for Scotch whisky? In July, the U.S. finally lifted its 15 month tariff on Scotch, one that had contributed to a 15 percent decline in exports to this country, one of Scotland’s biggest international markets.
takeaways: US lifted a 15-month tariff on Scotch in July 2026, reversing a 15 percent export decline to one of Scotland's largest markets.
A July 2026 UK-India free trade agreement opened access to the world's largest whisky market, potentially transforming Scotch sales abroad.
Diageo and Brown-Forman operations remain paused as post-pandemic oversupply and a historic liquid glut persist; distilleries like Clynelish closed visitor centers due to weak tourism.

MARKET.head: Trump bans Canadian alcohol imports as tariff war escalates
MARKET.summ: On Tuesday, president Donald Trump announced a plan to ban import of a range of Canadian products, escalating the already tense tariff disputes between the U.S. and its neighbor to the north. The restrictions , which are set to go into effect on Sept.
takeaways: President Trump announced a ban on Canadian alcohol imports effective September 29, escalating tariffs that began in April 2024 and July 2025.
Canada retaliated with levies on $20 billion of US goods starting Tuesday, prompting Trump's ban announcement.
US wine, beer, and spirits exporters faced considerable revenue losses in 2025 after Canada's retail and bar ban on US alcohol products.

CULTURE.head: AriZona Iced Tea launches artist residency at New York headquarters
CULTURE.summ: Any marketing executive will tell you that they care about their brand’s aesthetics, but it’s rare to find a corporation where the design language is as distinctive, long-lasting, and personal as AriZona Iced Tea , a commitment that has recently taken an unexpected turn. AriZona Iced Tea entered the market in 1992 with cans...
takeaways: AriZona Iced Tea, founded in 1992, launched a six-week artist residency program at its Woodbury, New York headquarters, hosting four artists per session since July 2025.
Residents receive stipends, living space, materials, and access to The Lookout studio and rooftop workspace to develop personal projects alongside company creatives.
Artists' work draws inspiration from AriZona's visual identity, with finished pieces exhibited and sometimes added to the company's permanent collection.

SCIENCE.head: Early harvests reshape winemaking, tourism, and costs across global regions
SCIENCE.summ: Along with high temperatures, wine regions around the world reported new records for early grape harvests this summer. For some, it was weeks ahead of the traditional fall schedule, for others it was months in advance. In the heart of the Roussillon in France, Domaine Lafage started picking grapes on July 23, something...
takeaways: Domaine Lafage in Roussillon began harvest on July 23, weeks earlier than traditional fall schedules; California Central Coast grower Kevin Merrill reported the earliest date in 27 years, six to eight weeks ahead of historical norms.

Early harvests force wineries to refrigerate and process fruit during peak summer electricity prices instead of cooler fall, raising costs; shorter harvest windows strain crews, custom crush facilities, and glass bottle supplies tied to heat-dependent furnaces.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Boycott Wines Grown With Herbicides
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Putting Adam Huss’s campaign into practice at the Austrian Single Vineyard Summit
NEWSLETTERS.author: Simon J. Woolf
takeaways: Adam Huss launched a campaign in August to boycott all wines produced with herbicides, arguing they degrade soil health and decrease wine quality.

Luís Patrão from Vadio in Bairrada, Portugal reported that his parents' generation's herbicide use turned vineyards into barren wastelands and eliminated local ladybird, eel, and salamander populations.

The author attended the Austrian Single Vineyard Summit in Grafenegg and used producer certifications (Organic, Biodynamic, Sustainable Austria) to select only herbicide-free wines from 556 offerings.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Sicus: distinctive low-intervention wines from Catalunya
NEWSLETTERS.summ: I popped into Dynamic Vines in Bermondsey on a Saturday morning and they were showing the wines of
NEWSLETTERS.author: Jamie Goode
takeaways: Sicus, Eduard Piè's winery near Tarragona, Catalunya, ferments indigenous varieties in local clay amphora, some buried in vineyards, using organic farming and no-till practices.
Sicus Cartoixà Brisat (Xarel.lo, 2019) scored 94/100 for its stony citrus, orange peel, and bright tangy profile.
Sicus Sumoi (2021) from El Roldonar vineyard features whole-bunch fermentation, 3 months amphora and 5 months stainless steel aging, at just 10% alcohol.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Is That the Death Rattle of Wine Writing I Hear?
NEWSLETTERS.summ: The purpose of any honest writing competition can only be to support and encourage the craft and industry of writing
NEWSLETTERS.author: Alder Yarrow

NEWSLETTERS.head: The Pluralism Of Wine Writing
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Einstein was there before us. As he famously put it, I know not with what technologies the third 67 Pall Mall awards were fought, but the fourth will be fought with quills and inkwells. Perhaps entrants will be invited to nearby Westminster school and asked to produce their submissions in real time.
NEWSLETTERS.author: Tim Atkin MW
takeaways: A winning entry in the Pall Mall awards' short-form writing competition faced allegations of AI use, with organizers defending it as 'not 100% AI-generated.'.
Tim Atkin argues wine writing encompasses journalism, criticism, and travelogues of varying quality, with no single definition or standard.
Atkin contends that wine writing's pluralism, allowing diverse voices and styles, is both its defining characteristic and greatest strength.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Heading Out
NEWSLETTERS.summ: Preparing to jump to Italy next week, plus this week’s favorite stories about food, wine, and culture
NEWSLETTERS.author: Meg Maker
takeaways: Meg Maker travels to Piemonte next week for a press tour of Roero, tasting wines alongside handmade foods including cheese, truffle, hazelnut, and honey.
Sarah Marsh MW argued at the Old Vine Conference in Napa that old vines are not universally superior; many carry viruses and can be less resilient than young vines.
Michelin issued its first wine producer ratings for Burgundy in July, followed by Bordeaux ratings this month, prompting analysis from Master Sommelier Dustin Wilson on the brand's motives.

NEWSLETTERS.head: Of Substack & wine
NEWSLETTERS.summ: All that’s being poured for your reading enjoyment in what is currently the most dynamic platform for wine media
NEWSLETTERS.author: Miquel Hudin
takeaways: Substack created a Wine & Spirits subsection within its Rising and Top lists, separating wine writing from the broader Food & Drink category for better discovery.
Miquel Hudin updated the Wine Substack List (WineStack) to require paid subscriptions in active use and human-written text only, excluding AI-generated content like 'Thirst Behavior' by Bodhi Landa.
Matthew Jukes, a traditional wine media writer, passed away last month.
